name: Brownish Pink
lede: Brownish Pink is a dusty pink, close to what dictionaries call nude, and its name is plain description.

sections.title: Pink, with brown in it
sections.body:
The name qualifies [[pink]] with brown, and our sources list it in the 2010 xkcd survey [1]. The nearest ISCC-NBS name is "dark yellowish pink" at a distance of 2.4 [1]. Compare [[rose-pink]], [[dusty-rose]] and [[rosy-brown]].

Paterson defines nude as a brownish pink and cites The Times of 1 March 2000 on Dior's nude-coloured chiffon dresses [2]. The same dictionary says tea rose is a yellowish pink, sometimes a brownish pink, and notes that Maerz and Paul advised against using the term [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch appears in 119 of our 23,781 paintings, 0.5 percent, as photographed [4]. It peaks in the 1900s, found in 11 of the 1,674 paintings from that century, 3.2 times the expected rate [4]. The most devoted painter is Henri Matisse, with 4 of his 50 works here, 6.8 times the baseline of the museums those works come from [4].
